clue.text: Mind about boy pinching answer

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip tightly, so the preceding pair of words closes around what follows

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A worry about a lad who keeps snatching the answers to a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: RE plus SON together grip the A: RE(A)SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason is the thinking faculty, a synonym for the mind or intellect.

clue.text: I study in peace in local

indicators.note: the second 'in' places one group of letters inside another word

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Someone describing how they read quietly in their neighbourhood pub, the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like the pub, but here it is a noun for someone who lives nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a person who lives in the area, which is what a resident is.

clue.text: Start to play a part, Evita, nervously

indicators.note: acting nervously means jittering about, so the name's letters are jumbled

parts.note: to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: An actress anxiously begins a role in the musical Evita.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate a machine or process is to start it, set it going.

clue.text: Duck with grim smell

parts.note: a duck is a zero in cricket, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: A cooked duck giving off an unpleasant, grim smell.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent, usually a noticeable one, synonymous with smell.

clue.text: Peer got harassed close to one female ward

indicators.note: being harassed means being harried and disturbed, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: these seven letters are rearranged along with the next one

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A nobleman pestered a young woman placed under his guardianship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female ward' must be read as one phrase: it is the definition, which is why the answer carries the feminine extra E.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégée is a woman under the guidance and protection of a patron, like a ward.

clue.text: I adore joiner working in port

indicators.note: something working is in operation and moving, so these letters are set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confessing a crush on a carpenter on the job at the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian seaport city on Guanabara Bay.

clue.text: Informer set up boy wearing hat

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A grass frames a lad who has a hat on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hat' looks like part of the wordplay with 'wearing', but it is the definition: a tarpaulin was a sailor's tarred hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is an old word for a sailor's waterproof hat made of tarred cloth.

clue.text: Swelling, blood covering it

indicators.note: something covering another wraps round it, so one word encloses the next

explanation.surface: A wound that has swollen up and is covered with blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is a swelling of the neck caused by an enlarged thyroid gland.

clue.text: Still supporting the Spanish sports team?

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word supporting another holds it up from underneath, so it is placed below

parts.note: even, as in 'even better', means still

explanation.surface: A query whether some team still backs Spanish players.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts EVEN underneath EL. The question mark flags that eleven defines the team by its size.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has eleven players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: TV series — it's funny, endless tease

indicators.note: funny here means odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order
without an end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to tease wool or hair is to comb it

explanation.surface: A television show described as amusing, with some never-ending ribbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' and 'tease' sound like a review of a comedy, but funny shuffles IT'S and tease is COMB losing its B.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom, or situation comedy, is a type of TV series.

clue.text: Girl from a French region

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a female first name
second meaning: an area in north-eastern France

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a girl hailing from a French region, but the name and the region are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a woman's given name and the historic region of north-east France bordering Germany.

clue.text: Former PM defends town

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782

explanation.surface: An ex-Prime Minister standing up for a place.
explanation.walkthrough: North Shields is a town on the River Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: North Shields is a town on Tyneside, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: Daughter has more than only fish

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter has more than just one fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a prized European flatfish, so it is a kind of fish.

clue.text: See eye to eye with a -conservationist? Not quite

indicators.note: falling just short means the word stops one letter before its end

parts.note: a Green is an environmental campaigner

explanation.surface: Asking whether one almost shares an environmentalist's views.
explanation.walkthrough: A GREEN loses its final N.
explanation.definitionFit: To see eye to eye with someone is to share their opinion, an idiom for concurring.

clue.text: Path through the countryside an utter liar portrayed differently

indicators.note: depicted in another way, so these letters are presented in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rural walk is described one way by an outright liar and otherwise by everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A nature trail is a signposted route through the countryside for observing wildlife.

clue.text: Near tower, diseased mountain ash

indicators.note: something diseased is unsound and out of shape, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A sickly mountain ash growing close to a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountain ash is another common name for the rowan tree, a synonym.

clue.text: Car thief brings girl, on one condition?

parts.note: a rider is an added condition or proviso

explanation.surface: A car thief turns up with a young woman, but only on a single condition.
explanation.walkthrough: A rider is a clause added to a contract or verdict, which is why it can mean a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A joyrider steals a car to drive it for fun, so is a kind of car thief.

clue.text: Flower girl in 1930s dance troupe?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a blue woodland spring flower
second meaning: one of the ... Girls, a Paris dance troupe founded in 1932

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower girl' looks like a wedding role; split it. The Bluebell Girls were a famous troupe of tall dancers in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a woodland plant with blue bell-shaped blooms and a member of the Bluebell Girls.

clue.text: Jumping style shown off in horse opera part, reportedly

parts.note: horse opera is a jokey name for a cowboy film

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so what counts is how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: a role is a part in a film

explanation.surface: An equestrian display seen in a cowboy show, as rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: The western roll is an old high-jump technique, rolling over the bar side-on.
explanation.definitionFit: The western roll is a high-jump technique, so it is a style of jumping.

clue.text: UK group steps in in US city

indicators.note: stepping in means entering, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra, a British band
pas is the French dance term for a step, plural unchanged

explanation.surface: A British band strides out in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is part of 'steps in'; the second is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: El Paso is a city in western Texas on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Chess piece thrown by the Parisian

explanation.surface: A chess piece hurled across the board by a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Castle is the common alternative name for the rook in chess.

clue.text: Humorist with name to memorise

parts.note: Edward Lear, Victorian writer of nonsense verse and limericks
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A comic writer has a name worth remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn lines is to commit them to memory, a synonym for memorise.

clue.text: Held back popular book

parts.note: to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A best-selling book kept off the shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept in reserve is held back for later use.

clue.text: Box squadron's leader, of more than average height

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: tall means of above average height

explanation.surface: A tall squadron leader takes up boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a verb about fighting; it is a noun for a compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A stall is a compartment for one animal in a stable, a kind of box.

clue.text: Behind the whole lot, when push comes to shove

explanation.surface: Someone at the back of a crowd that is pushing and shoving.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms meaning in the end or when everything is considered.

clue.text: Lumber theologian placed in auction

indicators.note: placing something in another puts it inside, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: Timber offered at auction by a man of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lumber' looks like timber but is a verb meaning to burden.
explanation.definitionFit: To lumber someone with a task is to burden them, which is to saddle them with it.

clue.text: How eggs may be served if done slowly

parts.note: as in 'go easy', gently and slowly

explanation.surface: Eggs come out a certain way if cooked gently.
explanation.walkthrough: Over easy is an American term for eggs fried on both sides with the yolk still runny.
explanation.definitionFit: Over easy describes fried eggs flipped briefly, a way of serving them.

clue.text: Female, 50, has spoken of a Roman goddess

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old woman has talked about an ancient Roman deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora was the Roman goddess of flowers, so floral can mean belonging to her.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral literally relates to Flora, the Roman goddess of flowering plants.
